items.title: False alarms are not measured by any review
items.whyItMatters: A triage rule sends patients with raised lactate to resuscitation; pathway studies hint at crowding but none measured harm to other patients.
items.opportunity: Derive the false-alarm proportion from reported accuracy at local prevalence and report it as a balancing outcome.

items.title: Overlap makes reviews look more consistent than the evidence is
items.whyItMatters: With a corrected covered area of 18 percent (c3), counting reviews would count the same studies again.
items.opportunity: Build a citation matrix and report each primary study once.

items.title: Older patients and people on beta blockers are falsely reassured more often
items.whyItMatters: A normal lactate misleads more often in these groups (retrieved pooled analysis).
items.opportunity: Extract subgroup findings by age and medication from each review.

items.title: Capillary values are read against venous thresholds
items.whyItMatters: Capillary lactate runs slightly higher and diverges at high values.
items.opportunity: Record sample type for each review and flag thresholds derived from venous or arterial samples.

items.title: Confidence in the reviews is mostly critically low
items.whyItMatters: Conclusions resting on low-confidence reviews should not drive a firm rule (c4).
items.opportunity: Rate each review and carry the rating into every conclusion.

errorsFound: The need treats 'sepsis' and 'death' as interchangeable outcomes; reviews of accuracy for sepsis with organ dysfunction and reviews of mortality answer different questions and must be synthesised separately.
reevaluation: The gaps confirm an umbrella review with outcomes chosen for the triage decision, overlap correction and confidence ratings.
summary: Five gaps; unmeasured false alarms and overlap are high severity.
